judgments.reasoning_cat1: The phrase "exclusive jurisdiction of the State of New York" is ambiguous as to whether it designates a sovereign (permitting federal courts sitting in New York) or only New York state courts, and "such court" has no antecedent since no court was named — a clear mechanical/lexical defect. The second sentence preserving removal rights compounds the uncertainty about whether federal forums are available.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This clause sits directly against the Service of Suit Endorsement (No. 15), which promises submission to "any court of competent jurisdiction" at the insured's request, and against the endorsement's non-variation clause, creating an evident conflict over exclusivity of the New York forum.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be readily reconciled with Section IX.I's exclusive New York jurisdiction clause, and the endorsement's own non-variation sentence deepens rather than resolves that tension.
